launch-ga-atlanta-piedmont-park.summary: Atlanta's signature urban park pairs skyline lawns and Lake Clara Meer with playgrounds, a free seasonal splash pad, a paid seasonal pool, dog parks, sports, gardens, events, and a direct BeltLine connection.
launch-ga-atlanta-piedmont-park.hours: Open daily 6:00 a.m.-11:00 p.m. Restrooms generally operate 8:00 a.m.-6:00 p.m.; pool, splash pad, courts, concessions, events, and other facilities use separate schedules.
launch-ga-atlanta-piedmont-park.parking: Use the shared paid, cashless Piedmont Park and Atlanta Botanical Garden garage at 1322 Monroe Drive, or arrive by MARTA, bike, or the BeltLine. Event days can fill the garage and change access.
launch-ga-atlanta-piedmont-park.arrival: Choose the entrance nearest your destination: Charles Allen Drive for the south-central park, Monroe Drive and the garage for northern destinations, or the BeltLine for the east side.
launch-ga-atlanta-piedmont-park.restrooms: Officially listed near Greystone, Noguchi Playscape, Legacy Fountain, tennis center, dog park, Charles Allen Gate, and behind Magnolia Hall; general restroom hours are 8:00 a.m.-6:00 p.m.
launch-ga-atlanta-piedmont-park.cost: General park access, lawns, paths, playgrounds, dog parks, and Legacy Fountain are free. Parking, pool admission, rentals, food, programs, and ticketed events cost separately.
launch-ga-atlanta-piedmont-park.accessibility: Major paved routes and the shared garage support accessible arrival, but slopes, crowds, festivals, and destination-specific entrances matter; use the official map for the shortest route.
launch-ga-atlanta-piedmont-park.dogs: Leashed dogs are welcome in general park areas and may be off leash only in the designated fenced dog parks; dogs are excluded from playgrounds, lake, courts, fields, pool areas, and some festivals.
launch-ga-atlanta-piedmont-park.family: Strong family choice with Noguchi Playscape, Mayor's Grove, Legacy Fountain, lake paths, lawns, and seasonal pool; the park is large, so navigate to the exact destination.
launch-ga-atlanta-piedmont-park.transit: Midtown and Arts Center MARTA stations are common rail approaches; local buses, bike routes, and the Eastside Trail also connect to the park.
launch-ga-atlanta-piedmont-park.need: Restrooms and water play close earlier than the park. Major festivals can control entrances, close lawns, restrict pets, and overwhelm parking, so check the event calendar before a time-sensitive visit.

launch-ga-atlanta-centennial-olympic-par.address: 265 Park Avenue West NW, Atlanta, GA 30313
launch-ga-atlanta-centennial-olympic-par.summary: Downtown Atlanta's Olympic legacy park centers on the Fountain of Rings and links major visitor attractions, gathering lawns, memorials, public art, gardens, and transit.
launch-ga-atlanta-centennial-olympic-par.hours: Open daily 7:00 a.m.-11:00 p.m. Fountain of Rings shows are scheduled daily at noon, 2:30 p.m., 6:30 p.m., and 9:00 p.m., subject to events, weather, and maintenance.
launch-ga-atlanta-centennial-olympic-par.parking: Use nearby paid downtown decks or transit rather than expecting park parking. Prices and street closures vary sharply during conventions, games, concerts, and festivals.
launch-ga-atlanta-centennial-olympic-par.arrival: The park spans several downtown blocks; use the Fountain of Rings or Visitor Center as a clear meeting point and choose the edge nearest your surrounding attraction.
launch-ga-atlanta-centennial-olympic-par.restrooms: Confirm the current public restroom location with the Visitor Center or your adjacent attraction; do not assume every surrounding venue allows non-ticketed restroom access.
launch-ga-atlanta-centennial-olympic-par.cost: Park admission and Fountain of Rings viewing are free. Surrounding attractions, parking, food, tours, and special events charge separately.
launch-ga-atlanta-centennial-olympic-par.accessibility: Broad paved paths and level plazas support wheeled mobility; event barricades and crowds can alter the easiest route.
launch-ga-atlanta-centennial-olympic-par.dogs: Leashed pets are allowed, with waste stations provided. Organized events can impose additional restrictions.
launch-ga-atlanta-centennial-olympic-par.family: The Fountain of Rings is the primary family draw, but show operations can pause for maintenance, weather, or events; bring a dry change of clothes if water interaction is allowed.
launch-ga-atlanta-centennial-olympic-par.transit: Peachtree Center MARTA is the closest heavy-rail approach, and the Atlanta Streetcar serves the park area; walking is often easier than moving a car among downtown attractions.
launch-ga-atlanta-centennial-olympic-par.need: Check the park calendar and Fountain of Rings status before promising children a water show. Biking, skating, scooters, organized sports, grills, alcohol, and glass are restricted inside the park.

launch-ga-atlanta-historic-fourth-ward-p.summary: A 17-acre BeltLine park with a dramatic stormwater lake, playground, seasonal splash pad, lawns, amphitheater, skatepark, shade structure, and direct Eastside Trail access.
launch-ga-atlanta-historic-fourth-ward-p.hours: City park hours are generally 6:00 a.m.-11:00 p.m. The splash pad is listed for 10:00 a.m.-8:00 p.m. from May 1 through October 1, subject to weather, maintenance, and seasonal changes.
launch-ga-atlanta-historic-fourth-ward-p.parking: Parking is limited and dispersed on surrounding streets and private decks. Walking, biking, rideshare, or arriving from the Eastside Trail is usually simpler on busy weekends.
launch-ga-atlanta-historic-fourth-ward-p.arrival: Use Dallas Street for the playground, splash pad, and upper park; use the BeltLine and skatepark access for the southern section. The lake sits below surrounding streets.
launch-ga-atlanta-historic-fourth-ward-p.restrooms: A fully accessible public restroom is listed near the Historic Fourth Ward Skatepark on the BeltLine; verify availability before relying on it for a young child.
launch-ga-atlanta-historic-fourth-ward-p.cost: Park, playground, splash pad, lake overlooks, lawns, skatepark, and BeltLine access are free. Nearby private parking, food, and events may charge.
launch-ga-atlanta-historic-fourth-ward-p.accessibility: Paved routes serve major areas, but the park drops substantially toward the basin; choose the nearest entrance to avoid unnecessary slopes.
launch-ga-atlanta-historic-fourth-ward-p.dogs: Leashed dogs are allowed under city rules; keep pets out of playground and splash-pad areas and clean up after them.
launch-ga-atlanta-historic-fourth-ward-p.family: Excellent for families because the playground, splash pad, shade structure, lawns, and lake paths sit in one destination; close supervision is important near water and slopes.
launch-ga-atlanta-historic-fourth-ward-p.transit: Reach via the Eastside Trail, local bus routes, bike, or rideshare; Midtown MARTA requires a longer walk or connection.
launch-ga-atlanta-historic-fourth-ward-p.need: The lake is stormwater infrastructure, not a swimming pond. The park's upper and lower areas feel separate, so route directly to the playground or skatepark rather than using only the general park pin.

launch-ga-atlanta-grant-park.summary: A historic, shaded neighborhood park surrounding Zoo Atlanta, with playgrounds, recreation center, seasonal pool, sports fields, walking paths, picnic areas, and major festivals.
launch-ga-atlanta-grant-park.hours: General city park hours are 6:00 a.m.-11:00 p.m. The recreation center, seasonal outdoor pool, Zoo Atlanta, fields, and reserved facilities use separate schedules.
launch-ga-atlanta-grant-park.parking: Free curbside and limited park-area parking compete with Zoo Atlanta and events. Use the zoo deck when visiting the zoo, and expect neighborhood congestion during festivals.
launch-ga-atlanta-grant-park.arrival: Choose Cherokee Avenue for zoo-side destinations and Park Avenue for recreation-center and pool access; the park is split by roads and large enough that the exact entrance matters.
launch-ga-atlanta-grant-park.restrooms: Restrooms are tied to the recreation center, pool, zoo, and event operations; confirm facility hours rather than assuming a building is open whenever the park is.
launch-ga-atlanta-grant-park.cost: The park, playgrounds, paths, fields when not reserved, and casual picnic areas are free. Zoo Atlanta, pool admission, reservations, food, and events may charge.
launch-ga-atlanta-grant-park.accessibility: Paved streets and paths reach major destinations, but historic grades, roots, and event closures can affect routes; use the destination entrance rather than crossing the full park.
launch-ga-atlanta-grant-park.dogs: Leashed dogs are allowed in general park areas but not inside Zoo Atlanta, pools, playgrounds, courts, or active fields; festivals may prohibit pets.
launch-ga-atlanta-grant-park.family: Strong family destination with playgrounds, pool, recreation center, open lawns, and Zoo Atlanta next door; plan the park and zoo as separate experiences with separate hours and fees.
launch-ga-atlanta-grant-park.transit: Local buses and rideshare serve the park; King Memorial MARTA is the nearest rail station but still requires a walk or connection.
launch-ga-atlanta-grant-park.need: Zoo traffic and festivals can transform parking and road access. The outdoor pool is seasonal, and recreation-center hours are not the same as park hours.

launch-ga-atlanta-westside-park.summary: Atlanta's largest park, commonly known as Westside Park, surrounds a former quarry reservoir with monumental entrances, overlooks, broad lawns, playgrounds, and paved walking and cycling routes.
launch-ga-atlanta-westside-park.hours: General city park hours are 6:00 a.m.-11:00 p.m.; gates, parking lots, reservoir overlooks, and reserved areas may close earlier or for operations.
launch-ga-atlanta-westside-park.parking: Use the free public lots at the Johnson Road or Grove Park entrances. Lots can fill for sunsets, weekends, and events, and the playground is a walk from parking.
launch-ga-atlanta-westside-park.arrival: Johnson Road is the most direct common arrival for the grand gateway, central lawns, playground route, and reservoir overlooks; confirm which entrance navigation selected.
launch-ga-atlanta-westside-park.restrooms: Public restrooms may be limited or tied to park facilities and events; plan conservatively and verify onsite signs before walking deep into the park.
launch-ga-atlanta-westside-park.cost: General park, overlooks, playground, lawns, and trails are free. Events, reservations, food, and special programs may charge.
launch-ga-atlanta-westside-park.accessibility: Wide paved paths serve major areas, but the park is very large and includes long grades. Visitors with limited stamina should route to the closest entrance and expect distance between parking, playground, and overlooks.
launch-ga-atlanta-westside-park.dogs: Leashed dogs are allowed under city park rules; keep pets out of playgrounds and restricted reservoir infrastructure.
launch-ga-atlanta-westside-park.family: The playground and lawns are family-friendly, but distances are longer than the map may suggest and reservoir edges are not water-access areas.
launch-ga-atlanta-westside-park.transit: MARTA's Bankhead station and local buses serve the broader area, but the final approach may require a walk or rideshare; cycling connections continue to expand.
launch-ga-atlanta-westside-park.need: The reservoir is protected drinking-water infrastructure: swimming, boating, shoreline access, and climbing barriers are prohibited. Bring water and sun protection because long paved sections are exposed.

launch-ga-atlanta-chastain-park.address: 140 West Wieuca Road NW, Atlanta, GA 30342
launch-ga-atlanta-chastain-park.summary: A large north Atlanta recreation complex with a popular PATH loop, playground, pool, tennis, golf, horse park, arts center, sports fields, amphitheater, and picnic areas.
launch-ga-atlanta-chastain-park.hours: General city park hours are 6:00 a.m.-11:00 p.m. The amphitheater may operate until 1:00 a.m. on performance nights; pool, tennis, golf, arts, and other facilities have separate schedules.
launch-ga-atlanta-chastain-park.parking: Parking is distributed among facility lots and roadside areas. Concerts, tournaments, and golf operations can change access dramatically, so navigate to the exact facility rather than the general park pin.
launch-ga-atlanta-chastain-park.arrival: Use West Wieuca Road for the playground and central recreation areas; other facilities have separate entrances around the park perimeter.
launch-ga-atlanta-chastain-park.restrooms: Restrooms are primarily associated with staffed facilities, playground areas, pool, tennis, golf, and events; hours vary by destination.
launch-ga-atlanta-chastain-park.cost: General park paths and playground access are free. Pool, tennis, golf, amphitheater events, classes, reservations, and concessions charge separately.
launch-ga-atlanta-chastain-park.accessibility: Major facilities have paved approaches, but the park is broad and rolling. Select the exact destination and parking lot before arrival.
launch-ga-atlanta-chastain-park.dogs: Leashed dogs are allowed on general park paths but excluded from pool, courts, golf course, playgrounds, fields, and event-controlled areas.
launch-ga-atlanta-chastain-park.family: The playground, PATH loop, seasonal pool, picnic areas, and sports make this useful for families, but it functions as several facilities rather than one compact park.
launch-ga-atlanta-chastain-park.transit: Bus service reaches the area, but most visitors drive or use rideshare; verify the correct gate for ticketed amphitheater events.
launch-ga-atlanta-chastain-park.need: Concert traffic and road controls can affect the entire park. Facility hours and admission are separate from general park hours, and the walking loop crosses busy access points.

launch-ga-atlanta-freedom-park.address: Freedom Parkway NE and Moreland Avenue NE, Atlanta, GA 30307
launch-ga-atlanta-freedom-park.summary: A linear arts and trails park connecting the Carter Center, Candler Park, Inman Park, Little Five Points, and the BeltLine through lawns, sculptures, and PATH routes.
launch-ga-atlanta-freedom-park.hours: General city park hours are 6:00 a.m.-11:00 p.m. Adjacent institutions, restrooms, events, and parking lots have separate schedules.
launch-ga-atlanta-freedom-park.parking: There is no single central park lot. Use legal neighborhood parking, the Carter Center area when visiting it, transit, bike, or a BeltLine connection; avoid blocking residential streets.
launch-ga-atlanta-freedom-park.arrival: Pick a destination first: Carter Center overlooks, Moreland Avenue meadow, Little Five Points, or the BeltLine junction. A general pin can leave you far from the intended segment.
launch-ga-atlanta-freedom-park.restrooms: Do not assume a public restroom is available along every trail segment. Use confirmed facilities at an open adjacent institution or the new BeltLine restroom network where applicable.
launch-ga-atlanta-freedom-park.cost: Park lawns, trails, and outdoor art are free. The Carter museum, private parking, food, and special events may have separate fees.
launch-ga-atlanta-freedom-park.accessibility: Paved PATH trails cover much of the linear park, but road crossings, grades, and long distances between destinations require route planning.
launch-ga-atlanta-freedom-park.dogs: Leashed dogs are welcome under city rules; keep them away from memorials, programmed spaces, and private grounds.
launch-ga-atlanta-freedom-park.family: Good for biking, walking, lawns, and public art, but it is a linear park with road crossings rather than a contained playground destination.
launch-ga-atlanta-freedom-park.transit: MARTA buses, bike routes, the Eastside Trail, and neighborhood walking connections are practical; rail stations are not immediately adjacent.
launch-ga-atlanta-freedom-park.need: Freedom Park is fragmented by streets and parkways. Use the specific landmark or trail junction in navigation, and bring lights if your return may occur near dusk.

launch-ga-atlanta-eastside-trail.address: Atlanta Beltline Eastside Trail, Atlanta, GA
launch-ga-atlanta-eastside-trail.summary: The BeltLine's busiest finished trail connects Piedmont Park, Ponce City Market, Historic Fourth Ward Park, Freedom Park, Inman Park, Krog Street, public art, food, and transit links.
launch-ga-atlanta-eastside-trail.hours: The trail follows City of Atlanta park hours, generally 6:00 a.m.-11:00 p.m. Adjacent businesses, parks, restrooms, and access gates use their own schedules.
launch-ga-atlanta-eastside-trail.parking: There is no single official trail lot. Use transit, bike, rideshare, legal street parking, or paid decks near your chosen access point; Ponce and Krog areas are busiest.
launch-ga-atlanta-eastside-trail.arrival: Choose an access point based on what you want to see. Piedmont-to-Ponce and Ponce-to-Krog are distinct walks, and the full corridor is longer than a casual visit.
launch-ga-atlanta-eastside-trail.restrooms: Accessible public restrooms are listed near Piedmont Park, Lowery-Bedford Pine, and Historic Fourth Ward Skatepark; availability can change, so check the official trail page.
launch-ga-atlanta-eastside-trail.cost: Trail access, public art, and connected city parks are free. Private parking, food, rentals, attractions, and events cost separately.
launch-ga-atlanta-eastside-trail.accessibility: The paved multi-use trail is broadly accessible, but crowds, crossings, grades at access ramps, construction, and fast-moving users can complicate travel.
launch-ga-atlanta-eastside-trail.dogs: Leashed dogs are allowed; keep a short leash in crowded sections and avoid blocking the path.
launch-ga-atlanta-eastside-trail.family: Stroller and bike friendly, with playgrounds and splash pads in connected parks, but the central trail can be extremely crowded and is not a contained play space.
launch-ga-atlanta-eastside-trail.transit: MARTA rail plus local bus, streetcar, bike share, and neighborhood connections can reach different segments; select the access point before choosing transit.
launch-ga-atlanta-eastside-trail.need: Stay right, pass predictably, and stop off the travel lane. Crowds peak around Ponce City Market and Krog Street, and construction can reroute access.

launch-ga-atlanta-cascade-springs-nature.summary: A shaded urban nature preserve with a waterfall, boardwalks, forest trails, Utoy Creek, a moss-covered springhouse, historic earthworks, picnic areas, and wildlife.
launch-ga-atlanta-cascade-springs-nature.hours: The preserve is open daily during city park hours, but the parking gate may close much earlier than the park; current visitor guidance has listed 3:00 p.m. weekdays and 7:30 p.m. weekends for the vehicle gate.
launch-ga-atlanta-cascade-springs-nature.parking: Use the free lot at 2852 Cascade Road and read the gate-closing sign before hiking. A late return can leave a vehicle behind a locked gate.
launch-ga-atlanta-cascade-springs-nature.arrival: Start at the Cascade Road parking lot trailhead. The waterfall and springhouse are reached on wooded paths and boardwalks rather than from a roadside overlook.
launch-ga-atlanta-cascade-springs-nature.restrooms: A new accessible public restroom has been installed at the preserve, but verify current hours and access onsite before relying on it.
launch-ga-atlanta-cascade-springs-nature.cost: Preserve, trails, waterfall, picnic areas, and parking are free.
launch-ga-atlanta-cascade-springs-nature.accessibility: The entrance area and some boardwalk portions are improved, but natural trails include roots, mud, slopes, creek edges, and potentially slippery surfaces; not every landmark has a step-free route.
launch-ga-atlanta-cascade-springs-nature.dogs: Leashed dogs are welcome; keep them out of waterways and under control around wildlife and narrow trails.
launch-ga-atlanta-cascade-springs-nature.family: A memorable short nature outing for children who can manage uneven trails, but close supervision is essential around slippery rocks, water, and drop-offs.
launch-ga-atlanta-cascade-springs-nature.transit: Bus access is limited compared with central Atlanta parks; driving or rideshare is most practical, but confirm pickup signal and gate timing.
launch-ga-atlanta-cascade-springs-nature.need: Rocks near Cascade Falls and the creek can be slick, and water can move quickly after rain. Wear traction, avoid climbing wet rocks, and note the parking-gate closing time before leaving the lot.

launch-ga-atlanta-perkerson-park.summary: A 50-acre southwest Atlanta park with a free seasonal splash pad, large playground, disc golf, tennis, basketball, sports fields, pavilion, creek, and mature shade trees.
launch-ga-atlanta-perkerson-park.hours: General city park hours are 6:00 a.m.-11:00 p.m. Splash pad, fields, courts, reservations, and programs use seasonal or separate schedules.
launch-ga-atlanta-perkerson-park.parking: Free parking is available from Deckner Avenue and nearby park entrances, but lots and legal curb space can fill during tournaments, parties, and splash-pad weather.
launch-ga-atlanta-perkerson-park.arrival: Use the Deckner Avenue side for the playground and splash pad; disc-golf holes and sports areas spread across the larger park.
launch-ga-atlanta-perkerson-park.restrooms: Restroom availability can depend on recreation, event, or portable facilities; confirm before a long family visit.
launch-ga-atlanta-perkerson-park.cost: Park, playground, seasonal splash pad, casual courts, trails, and disc golf are free. Reservations, organized programs, and events may charge.
launch-ga-atlanta-perkerson-park.accessibility: The toddler playground includes ramp access and play areas use resilient surfacing, but disc golf and natural park sections include uneven terrain.
launch-ga-atlanta-perkerson-park.dogs: Leashed dogs are allowed in general areas but excluded from playground, splash pad, courts, and active fields.
launch-ga-atlanta-perkerson-park.family: One of the city's stronger free warm-weather family parks because the playground and splash pad share the same destination; bring shade and verify water operation.
launch-ga-atlanta-perkerson-park.transit: Local buses serve the surrounding area; driving or rideshare is usually simplest for families carrying water-play supplies.
launch-ga-atlanta-perkerson-park.need: The splash pad is seasonal and can close for maintenance or weather. Disc golf crosses wooded terrain, so watch for flying discs and do not use fairways as picnic areas.
